acme-sre: Hi team — hitting an intermittent failure on embeddings endpoint since last deploy. ~1% of calls return vectors with the wrong dimension and our indexer crashes. Example: expected 1024, got 1536. Happens across Python and TS clients. Request ID: trace_0x7f3a9c. Any ideas?

lydia-support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste a minimal repro (request body + headers) and approximate timestamps?

acme-sre: Minimal repro below. Happens with batch sizes 1..8, more likely when we hit higher concurrency. Timestamps: 2026-05-02T14:22:10Z and 2026-05-02T14:24:33Z.

acme-sre: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v1","input":["hello","world"],"batch_size":4}'
```

acme-sre: Python SDK call we used: ```from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('TOKEN'))
client.embeddings.create(model="embed-large-v1", input=batch, timeout=15)```

acme-sre: Sample response (bad): `{\"data\":[{\"embedding\":[0.12,0.34,...(1536 floats total)...,0.01]}]}`

sarah-ng: Thanks — two quick hypotheses: 1) request is being routed to mixed model variants (1024 vs 1536 dim) due to fallback routing; 2) client-side batching/concatenation bug where responses from two different requests get merged.

josh-m: Can you also share what model id exactly (including version) you're sending? e.g. embed-large-v1 vs embed-large-v1-quant. The runtime can route to a quantized variant with different output dims if model aliasing is used.

acme-sre: We're passing exactly "embed-large-v1" — no explicit version suffix. We pinned it after the incident but the failures predate the pin.

kevin-infra: infra-bot: collected logs for trace_0x7f3a9c: upstream routed to node pool A -> served by model embed-large-v1@rev=2026-04-29 -> dim=1024. Another request same window routed to node pool B -> model embed-large-v1-quant@rev=2026-03-12 -> dim=1536. Looks like routing rules allowed variant mix under burst.

acme-sre: Whoa — so the same model alias can point to multiple variants during rollout? That explains mixed dims. But why would the server return 1536 for quant? We expected quant to preserve dim.

eng-ml: Not all quantized variants have identical output shapes if they were onboarded from different base model checkpoints. We should have flagged that.

lydia-support: Immediate mitigation: 1) pin the exact model revision in requests (model:"embed-large-v1@rev=2026-04-29"); 2) as a stopgap, validate vector lengths client-side and retry when length mismatches (log & drop to avoid indexer crash).

acme-sre: We implemented client-side length check + retry/backoff. But retries sometimes return the shorter/longer vector too. Any recommended backoff params?

josh-m: Use exponential backoff with full jitter. Start at 200ms, cap at 2s, max 5 attempts. Also include the model param on retry to pin it. Example pseudocode: ```for i in range(5): resp = call(model='embed-large-v1@rev=2026-04-29') if len(resp.embedding)==1024: break sleep = random()*min(200*(2**i),2000) time.sleep(sleep)```

kevin-infra: We're also going to add a server-side guarding check in the routing layer to avoid returning mixed-dim outputs for requests using the same alias within a short window. Will push a hotfix to routing policy to prefer model variants with matching embedding sizes.

acme-sre: Appreciate that. Two more things: 1) billing already charged full request for bad response (we get charged per request even if vector invalid) — can we get billing credit for the bad responses? 2) Any ETA for the roll-out fix?

lydia-support: For billing we'll submit a credit request — please DM me the affected invoice IDs and sample trace IDs. For ETA, infra says hotfix deploy to routing in next 24-48 hours, with monitoring for 72 hours after.

eng-ml: Follow-up: we found an older model onboarding that had a shape mismatch bug. We'll reconcile model catalog metadata to include embedding_dim as a required invariant and fail onboarding if mismatch. That should prevent future surprises.

acme-sre: Quick question on diagnostics — what headers or params should we collect next time to make triage faster?

kevin-infra: Collect request_id/trace_id (we got trace_0x7f3a9c), model param, client SDK/version, batch size, concurrency, and the whole raw response body. If possible, include tcp dump around the time for deep infra triage.

acme-sre: got it. We'll add additional logging and pin model rev for now. We'll open a follow-up ticket if we see more. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

lydia-support: I filed the billing ticket and created an internal ticket (INFR-1287) to track routing hotfix + catalog validations. Keeping this thread open until after 72h monitoring window.

infra-bot: Deploy started: routing-hotfix/2026-05-03T03:00Z by kevin-infra. Build 0.9.12 -> canary -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% rollout plan.

acme-sre: Noted, thanks. We'll monitor and report back if anything else pops up.

eng-ml: For SDK teams: putting an additional client-side validation in SDKs (Python/TS/Go) to warn on dimension mismatch before returning to user would be helpful — PR incoming.

sarah-ng: Great — will track SDK PR. Marking action items: (1) acme pins model rev + enable length check; (2) support issues billing credit; (3) infra routing hotfix rollout; (4) eng-ml catalog validation; (5) SDK teams add warnings.

acme-sre: Thanks everyone. Closing on our side unless we see more.
